docs.title: Pixel Legion Maker
docs.text:
A hero builder for small pixel-art characters in Unity 6. Combine parts, weapons and dyes in a play-mode editor, then use the result as a ready-to-play prefab, build heroes at runtime from a one-line recipe, or export frame sheets for any engine.

Every hero stands about 44 pixels tall (32 pixels per unit) on one shared bone rig, so all parts and weapons fit every hero and every motion.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Build heroes from 187 parts and 85 weapons and shields, 8 skin tones, 11 dye palettes and any custom color. The hero editor
  • Play them with 12 motions for each of 9 weapon styles, animation events for hit, cast and end, and projectiles. Heroes in code
  • Chain motions into named actions such as a three-hit combo, played by every hero with its own weapon style. Custom actions
  • Assemble heroes at runtime from recipes or random seeds. Runtime recipes
  • Export frame sheets with JSON metadata, and render crisp pixels with the included camera. Frame sheets and camera
  • Add your own art as PNG files in a content pack that package updates never touch. Content packs

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Item Requirement Unity 6000.0 or newer (developed and tested on 6000.0.47f1) Render pipeline Built-in or Universal (URP, including the 2D renderer). HDRP is not supported. Input Input Manager (old), Input System package, or both Packages uGUI (com.unity.ugui, in the default Unity templates) is required. 2D Sprite (com.unity.2d.sprite) is used when present for rebuilding the catalog but is not required. Test Framework is optional (for the included tests). Platforms Any platform that supports SpriteRenderer and Animator

Start with the Quick start.

First release: hero editor, 187 parts, 85 weapons, 55 example heroes, 12 motions (including walk and jump) for 9 weapon styles, dyes and custom colors, skin tones, animation events, custom actions, content packs, projectiles, runtime recipes, frame sheet export, pixel-perfect camera, Built-in and URP support.

docs.title: Content packs
docs.text: A content pack is a folder of parts, weapons, projectiles and heroes with a Content Pack asset at its top. The package itself is the pack LegionBasePack.asset. Keeping your own art in a pack of its own, outside Assets/PixelUnitStudio, keeps it apart from the package, so updating the package never touches it. Add-on packs for Pixel Legion Maker are packs too: they hold only art and heroes, and they need this package to work.

docs.title: Make a pack
docs.text:
1. Create a folder such as Assets/MyLegionPack/ and, inside it, Create > Pixel Legion Maker > Content Pack.
  2. Put images in the same layout as the package: Parts/<Slot>/, Weapons/, Projectiles/, and optionally WeaponTurns/ (24 pre-rotated turns of a weapon, same file name; without them the weapon art is rotated as is).
  3. Name files type first, as the package does (axe_frost, helmet_raider). The first word picks a weapon's motion style and its filter in the editor. A name the package or an earlier pack already uses is skipped with a warning.
  4. Give options card names under Titles on the pack asset. An option without one shows its file name, tidied (axe_frost → "Axe frost").

The catalog picks up the pack by itself the next time the editor is in focus.

docs.title: Pack fields
docs.text: Field Use Title Shown on the corner of the pack's part cards and over its heroes in the hero list Order Packs are read in this order (the package is 0, new packs 100) Parts / Weapons / Weapon Turns / Projectiles Folder Image folders, relative to the pack asset Heroes Folder Hero prefabs that come with the pack and their LegionActions.asset. The editor lists them under the pack's title; loading one and pressing Save puts a copy in your save folder. The pack's actions show in the Actions panel to play or copy Generated Folder Card icons made by the catalog build

docs.title: Custom actions
docs.text:
Actions in the editor's top bar chains motions into a named action, such as a three-hit combo or a channel-and-release spell.

  1. Press motions under Add step. Pressing the same motion again counts up its repeat; − / + change it later and ✕ removes the step (up to 12 steps, 9 repeats each).
  2. For Channel, the repeat is the number of channel loops before the next step (add Release after it).
  3. Play tries the action on the preview hero, Save Action stores it under its name (the same name replaces it), and clicking a saved action loads it for editing.

Actions name motions, not weapon styles, so one action plays on every hero with that hero's own version of each motion. They are kept in Units/LegionActions.asset, which every hero saved in that folder references. When an action ends the hero returns to idle, unless the last step is Death.

Five examples are included: Triple Strike, Charge, Leap Strike, Channeled Spell and Last Stand.

To play actions from your game, see Heroes in code.

docs.title: Your own parts and weapons
docs.text:
The catalog is built from the image files of every content pack in the project. When a pack is added or removed, or images are added to or removed from one, the catalog rebuilds itself the next time the editor is in focus; this takes under a minute. To rebuild by hand, for example after redrawing an image at the same size, run Tools > Pixel Legion Maker > Build Catalog.

Put your own art in a pack of your own outside Assets/PixelUnitStudio, so package updates never touch it.

docs.title: Parts
docs.text:
Parts go in Parts/<Slot>/<name>.png.

  • A part image is a 256×64 slot sheet that uses the same cell layout as the rig. See Rig/part_guide.png and Rig/body_template.png. Only fill the cells your slot draws (for example the Head cell for Hair, Mask and Ornament).
  • An optional <name>_full.png (the part drawn on the 29×42 full body, Rig/base_body_full.png) is used as the card icon.
  • Outline color is (16, 5, 5). Draw the character facing left.
  • Import settings: Sprite, point filter, no compression.

docs.title: Weapons
docs.text:
Weapons go in Weapons/<kind>_<name>.png.

  • One square image (48, 64, 80 or 96 pixels). The image center is the grip. The blade points left. See Rig/weapon_guide.png.
  • The first word of the file name picks the motion style: sword, axe, mace (default swing), spear, staff, bow, crossbow, gun, dagger, throw, and heavy weapons greatsword, greataxe, hammer, club, halberd, scythe. Names starting with shield are shields.
  • Keep one-handed weapons about 16–26 pixels from grip to tip so they stay above the ground in every motion.

docs.title: Projectiles
docs.text: Projectiles go in Projectiles/<style>_<name>.png (16×16, pointing left). The first word is the weapon style that shoots it: bow, crossbow, gun or staff.

docs.title: Dyeing
docs.text: Dyeing recolors the most common color group of a part with one of the dye palettes, keeping its light and shade steps.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Heroes look blurry. Use an orthographic camera with LegionPixelCamera, or a camera size that gives an integer pixel scale. Keep sprites on point filtering.

A part does not show in the editor. Check that the file is in the right Parts/<Slot>/ folder of a pack and that its name is not already used (the Console shows a warning), then run Tools > Pixel Legion Maker > Build Catalog.

Heroes face the wrong way. The rig faces left. Set the x scale of the hero root to −1 to face right.

An attack stays on its last frame. One-shot motions hold their last frame by design. Tick Return To Idle on LegionEvents, or play idle from your game code (Heroes in code).

The editor buttons do not react. The editor adds a UI input module that matches your input settings. If you replaced the EventSystem in the editor scene, keep one in the scene.

Does it work with URP? Yes. The dye shader is a plain sprite shader that renders in both the Built-in pipeline and URP, including the 2D renderer. HDRP is not supported.

Can I use the heroes outside Unity? Yes. Frame sheets are plain PNG files with JSON metadata.

Where do I report a bug? See Support and licenses.

docs.title: The hero editor
docs.text:
The editor is a play-mode tool (Scenes/LegionEditor.unity). Open it with Tools > Pixel Legion Maker > Open Editor and press Play. The screen has three columns.

  • Left: slots. Face: Eyes, Hair, Beard, Mask. Gear: Helmet, Ornament, Top, Pants, Armor, Cape. Weapons: Main hand, Off hand. Each row shows the current part.
  • Center: preview. The Skin row recolors the body and the skin drawn on parts (pale, tan, brown, dark, orc, undead, demon, frost); weapons keep their colors. Zoom with − / +, change the backdrop with Background, mirror with Flip. The buttons below play each motion. Pause and the slider step through frames.
  • Right: parts. All parts for the selected slot. Weapons can be filtered by kind. Swatches dye the selected part. + opens hue, saturation and brightness sliders for a custom color; the five light-to-dark shades are made from it.

docs.title: Top bar
docs.text: Button Action New Start from the default hero Randomize Random combination (seeded, always a valid hero) Undo Undo the last change Heroes Open the saved hero library (load, delete) Actions Open the custom action panel Copy / Paste Copy the hero as a recipe line to the clipboard, or apply a recipe from the clipboard Export Write the frame sheet of the current hero Save Save the hero as a prefab

docs.title: Weapons decide the pose
docs.text: The main hand is the attacking hand. Its weapon decides the motion style: sword swing, spear thrust, bow shot, staff cast, heavy two-handed slam, dagger, thrown weapon or firearm. The off hand holds a shield, a second weapon or a decorative item.

docs.title: Dyes and skin tones
docs.text: Dyeing recolors the most common color group of a part with a palette or a custom color, keeping its light and shade steps. Glow colors of the glowing eyes are kept when other parts are dyed.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Save writes Units/HERO_<NAME>.prefab. The hero library lists your heroes and, under their titles, the heroes of other content packs.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Import the package. Everything lives in Assets/PixelUnitStudio/.
  2. Choose Tools > Pixel Legion Maker > Open Editor and press Play.
  3. Pick a slot on the left (Eyes, Hair, Helmet, Main hand, ...), then a part on the right. Click a color swatch to dye the part, or + to mix any color. Pick a skin tone above the preview.
  4. Press Save and give the hero a name. The prefab is written to Assets/PixelUnitStudio/Units/HERO_<NAME>.prefab.
  5. Open Tools > Pixel Legion Maker > Open Game Sample and press Play to see saved heroes act in a scene.

55 example heroes are included in Units/ (knight, priest, ninja, witch, fencer, crusader, vampire, orc, fairy and more).

docs.title: Samples
docs.text:
Scene Shows Samples/LegionGameSample.unity Saved heroes attacking, shooting projectiles on hit events and playing custom actions Samples/LegionAssemblySample.unity Six heroes built at runtime from recipes and seeds; Shuffle rebuilds them and Dye recolors them

Open them with Tools > Pixel Legion Maker > Open Game Sample and Open Assembly Sample. Open Editor returns to the hero editor.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text: Tools > Pixel Legion Maker Does Open Editor Opens the hero editor scene Open Game Sample / Open Assembly Sample Opens a sample scene Online Documentation Opens this manual Build Catalog Rebuilds the part catalog by hand (it also rebuilds by itself, see Your own parts and weapons) Export Saved Hero Sheets Writes frame sheets for every saved hero (Frame sheets) Build Animations, Build Editor Scene, Import Rig and Open Preview Regenerate the clips, the editor scene and the rig preview

docs.title: Runtime recipes
docs.text:
Heroes can be built at runtime from the catalog (Generated/LegionCatalog.asset) without saved prefabs. A recipe is one line of Slot=part[:dye] pairs separated by spaces:

Helmet=helmet_mitre Cloth=robe_priest:gold Pant=pants_robe WeaponRight=staff_sun

using PixelUnitStudio;

var recipe = LegionRecipe.Parse(text);
foreach (var name in recipe.Missing(catalog)) Debug.LogWarning(name);
var hero = LegionBuilder.Create(catalog, recipe, parent);
hero.Play("attack");
hero.Choose("Helmet", "helmet_brim");   // swap a part (null clears the slot)
hero.Dye("Cloth", "azure");             // dye a slot (null restores the original colors)
hero.Dye("Hair", "#3A7BD5");            // any color as #RRGGBB
hero.SetSkin("orc");                    // skin tone (null for the original)
Destroy(hero.Root);
  • Slots you leave out are empty, or use their default part.
  • Skin=<tone> sets the skin tone, and a dye can be a palette name or #RRGGBB, for example Hair=hair_bun:#3A7BD5 Skin=tan.
  • LegionRecipe.Random(catalog, new System.Random(seed)) returns the same hero for the same seed.
  • LegionRecipe.From(unit) and LegionRecipe.From(builder) turn a saved prefab or a live hero back into a recipe (ToString()).
  • The Copy button in the editor gives you the recipe of the current hero.

Samples/LegionAssemblySample.unity builds six heroes from recipes and random seeds; Shuffle rebuilds them and Dye recolors them.

Slot names and dye names are listed in Slots, dyes and content.

docs.title: Slots and draw order (within the head)
docs.text:
Slot Content Layer Eye Eye color, glowing eyes 2 FaceHair Beards 4 Mask Face cloth, masks, faceplates 5 Hair Hair styles 6 Helmet Helmets, hats, hoods 8 Ornament Horns, halo, hair flower (shown over any hair or helmet) 9

Under a helmet that covers the head, tall hairstyles (crests, quiffs, buns, flames) switch to a trimmed version so nothing pokes through. The crown, headband and feather band leave the top open and keep the full hairstyle.

Body slots: Top (Cloth), Pants (Pant), Armor (Armor), Cape (Back). Weapon slots: Main hand (WeaponRight), Off hand (WeaponLeft). Recipes use the names in code font.

docs.title: Dye palettes and skin tones
docs.text:
Dyes: crimson, ember, gold, forest, teal, azure, violet, rose, brown, charcoal, ivory, or #RRGGBB for a custom color.

Skin tones: pale, tan, brown, dark, orc, undead, demon, frost.

Glow colors of the glowing eyes are kept when other parts are dyed, and change when the eyes themselves are dyed.

docs.title: Content
docs.text: Kind Count Parts 187 (Armor 14, Back 15, Top 19, Eyes 16, Beard 10, Hair 34, Helmet 27, Mask 18, Ornament 10, Pants 24) Weapons and shields 85 Example heroes 55 Motions 12 per weapon style, 9 weapon styles Dye palettes 11, plus any custom color Skin tones 8 Projectiles 4

docs.title: Frame sheet export
docs.text:
Export in the editor, or Tools > Pixel Legion Maker > Export Saved Hero Sheets, writes Exports/Heroes/HERO_<NAME>.png and a .json file next to it, in the project folder (outside Assets).

  • One row per motion, one column per frame, at 1:1 pixel size. Frames grow to fit large weapons.
  • The JSON lists fps, frameWidth, frameHeight, the foot origin (originX from the left, groundPx from the bottom) and clips (name, row, frame count, loop, and events with the hit, cast and end frames).

The sheets do not depend on Unity, so you can use them in other engines or tools.

docs.title: Pixel-perfect camera
docs.text:
Add LegionPixelCamera to an orthographic camera.

Field Meaning Pixels Per Unit 32 for hero art Reference Resolution The smallest view in art pixels. The screen always shows an integer multiple of it. Upscale Render Texture In play mode, render at art resolution and scale up by an integer factor. Rotated limbs and weapons then snap to the pixel grid.

It works the same in the Built-in pipeline and URP. The game and assembly samples use it at 384×216.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
Start with the FAQ. Questions and bug reports: GitHub Issues, or email hyunter@flycat.co.kr.

Please include:

  • The Pixel Legion Maker version and your Unity Editor version.
  • The render pipeline and input backend you use.
  • Steps to reproduce the issue, the expected result and the actual result.
  • Relevant Console messages and, when useful, a screenshot.

docs.title: Heroes in code
docs.text:
A saved hero is a normal prefab with an Animator.

using PixelUnitStudio;

var hero = Instantiate(heroPrefab);
hero.transform.localScale = new Vector3(-1, 1, 1);   // the rig faces left; flip to face right
var unit = hero.GetComponent<LegionUnit>();
unit.Play("attack");
  • Motions: idle, running (run), walk, jump, attack, damaged, death, cast, stun, and the channel set cast_start → cast_loop → cast_end. jump jumps in place; move the hero from your game code.
  • LegionUnit.Play chooses the right version of the motion for the weapon kind (attack@spear, attack@bow, ...).
  • One-shot motions (attack, damaged, cast, cast_end, jump, death) stop on their last frame. Tick Return To Idle on the hero's LegionEvents component to go back to idle automatically (death stays down).
  • cast_start plays once and then loops cast_loop automatically. Play cast_end when the channel ends.

docs.title: Custom actions in code
docs.text:
Saved heroes carry a LegionActionPlayer that knows the actions made in the editor (Custom actions).

var actions = hero.GetComponent<LegionActionPlayer>();
actions.Play("Triple Strike");                      // false if the library has no such action
actions.Finished += action => Debug.Log(action.name + " done");

Hit and cast events fire for every step, so projectiles and damage work as with single motions. Return To Idle waits until the whole action ends. Playing a motion with LegionUnit.Play stops the action. Heroes built at runtime use builder.Actions (set its library, or pass a LegionAction to Play).

docs.title: Animation events
docs.text:
Every saved hero has a LegionEvents component. The clips call it at the moments a game needs:

Event When hit The attack connects: the blade lands, the arrow, bolt, bullet or orb leaves, the thrown weapon leaves the hand cast The spell is released (cast, and the end of cast_start) end The last frame of a one-shot motion 
var events = hero.GetComponent<LegionEvents>();
events.returnToIdle = true;
events.Fired += (name, state) => { if (name == LegionEvents.Hit) DealDamage(); };
// or wire onHit / onCast / onEnd in the inspector

The string state is the animator state, for example attack@bow.

docs.title: Projectiles
docs.text:
Bows, crossbows, guns and staves shoot a projectile sprite from Projectiles/ (arrow, bolt, bullet, orb). Thrown weapons fly as the weapon itself on an arc and spin through prebuilt turns, so pixels never smear.

events.Fired += (name, state) =>
{
    if (name != LegionEvents.Hit) return;
    var shot = LegionProjectile.Launch(catalog, unit, target.position);   // null for melee weapons
    if (shot != null) shot.Arrived += _ => DealDamage();
};

LegionProjectile.Launch(builder, target) does the same for heroes built at runtime. Projectiles snap to the 1-pixel grid and only fly; your game decides what they hit.

Use point filtering and an orthographic camera. See Pixel-perfect camera for crisp pixels at any screen size.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The generated API reference documents the public C# types and members in the package's two assemblies:

  • PixelUnitStudio.Runtime: heroes, the builder and recipes, events, actions, projectiles, the catalog and the pixel camera.
  • PixelUnitStudio.Editor: catalog build, animation build, frame sheet export and content packs.

Start with Heroes in code and Runtime recipes for examples. The C# namespace is PixelUnitStudio.

The reference is generated from the package's public declarations. The package implementation is not published with this site.
